title: Masala Mixtape Brings 18 South Asian Artists to The Matriarch in NYC
excerpt: The South Asian music festival returned for its fifth year on October 23, 2026, with hip-hop, pop, R&B, electronic and Bollywood acts, 10-plus vendors and tiered tickets from $20 to $80.
body:
• Masala Mixtape, New York's South Asian music festival, returned for its fifth year on Friday, October 23, 2026, at a new Manhattan venue, The Matriarch NYC in Hell's Kitchen.
  • The official listing promised 18 artists on one stage over more than five hours, spanning hip-hop, pop, R&B, electronic and Bollywood music, plus more than 10 vendors.
  • Tickets were tiered from a $20 pre-sale to $30 general admission, $40 final sale, $50 on the day and $80 VIP, sold through the official Handstamp page.
  • The festival was founded by Pankti Doshi with co-hosts Raghav Mehrish and Ramya Baratam to put South Asian talent, food and brands on one New York stage.

Masala Mixtape took over a new Manhattan home this fall. The South Asian music festival returned to New York City for its fifth year on Friday, October 23, 2026, moving to The Matriarch NYC in Hell's Kitchen with a lineup of 18 artists, more than 10 vendors and over five hours of music, according to its official Handstamp event page. The night ran from 7:00 p.m. to 2:00 a.m. EDT.

Plan Your Visit

  • Date: Friday, October 23, 2026
  • Time: 7:00 p.m. – 2:00 a.m. EDT
  • Venue: The Matriarch NYC
  • Address: 512 W 42nd St, New York, NY 10036
  • Admission: Pre-sale $20; general admission $30; final sale $40; day of $50; VIP $80
  • Tickets: Official Handstamp event page
  • Official page: Masala Mixtape '26 on Handstamp

What was on stage

The 2026 edition put 18 artists on one stage, with a programme spanning hip-hop, pop, R&B, electronic and Bollywood music, the listing said. Among the released artists on the official page were Shevya featuring RMS and Nory, Ben Parag, and Praveen Gunendran featuring Rad. Artist submissions for the lineup were closed ahead of the event, and the festival also listed more than 10 vendors alongside the music, continuing the format of pairing performances with South Asian food and brands built by South Asian creatives.

The October listing was also carried in SHOR New York's October 2026 guide to South Asian events in the city, which billed "Masala Mixtape '26" at The Matriarch NYC in Hell's Kitchen on Friday, October 23, with tickets through the same official page.

A festival built for South Asian talent

Masala Mixtape began as a festival dedicated to elevating South Asian talent in New York City. Pankti Doshi, who presents the festival, created it with co-hosts Raghav Mehrish and Ramya Baratam. "South Asian talent has been up and on the rise in the past decade. As music fans and event experts, we felt like we were in a position to create a space and support South Asian creatives," Doshi told Epicenter NYC at the festival's launch. "We didn't want to just be observers, but actually participate in moving the needle in South Asian representation."

"Our community has so much to offer in terms of creativity and talent so it's important we create a space and a platform to highlight these South Asian artists and brands."

— Pankti Doshi, co-founder, Masala Mixtape

Doshi has also pushed back on the idea that South Asian music means only film songs. "A common misconception people have about South Asian music is that it is only Bollywood music," she said. "Our artists are bringing in lots of different flavors of music to the festival. We are intentionally gathering a versatile portfolio to show the breadth of talent in this genre." That breadth is the through-line of the 2026 edition: one stage moving between hip-hop, pop, R&B, electronic sets and Bollywood across a single night in Midtown Manhattan.

Why it matters for New York's diaspora

Five editions in, Masala Mixtape has become a fixed date in New York's South Asian cultural calendar: a festival built by diaspora organisers, staged this year in Hell's Kitchen rather than Brooklyn, and designed as a place for South Asian Americans to hear their own artists headlining. For readers who missed the October 23 night, the official Handstamp page linked above is the organiser's listing for the festival and the first place its future editions are posted.
